entries: Request verification | Interpret examination requests and clinical information | Determine examination site, position and exposure conditions from radiologists' requests and clinical information, and verify patient identity and examination site.

Patient preparation | Position patients and communicate about safety | Explain examination procedures and cooperation requirements, position and immobilize patients for the examination site, and implement radiation protection and necessary care.

Equipment operation | Operate imaging equipment under specified conditions | Operate X-ray, CT and other imaging equipment, set exposure time and distance, and obtain images meeting diagnostic requirements.

Image quality evaluation | Check image quality needed for diagnosis | Evaluate whether images meet diagnostic purposes under technical standards, and document unacceptable images and reasons for repeats; this is not making a disease diagnosis.

Contrast procedures and assistance | Work under physician guidance | Prepare and use contrast agents or medications under radiologist guidance, assisting with more complex contrast and interventional procedures.

Records and quality control | Maintain records and report faults | Record examination and patient information, maintain examination protocol documents, perform quality control and report equipment abnormalities.

subject.name: Radiologic Technologists and Technicians
subject.summary: Radiologic technologists and technicians carry out X-ray, CT and other imaging work under examination requests and applicable protocols: identity and site checks, patient preparation and positioning, authorized exposure settings, image acquisition, technical image-quality evaluation and documentation. Technical evaluation is not disease diagnosis. Contrast-related duties require applicable legal and professional conditions and physician guidance. U.S. wages use exact occupation 29-2034; this page’s employment overview uses the combined radiologic and MRI group. Mainland China education, recruitment, professional-title qualifications and applicable radiation-worker requirements are considered separately; exact national or city occupational wages remain unavailable.
